style: Say brightly and cheerfully, like an upbeat first grade teacher.
lines: Soft balls only. Throw at the paper target on the wall, never at the screen, a TV or the laptop.

Tape a paper target on the wall, two big steps away from the screen. Draw three rings on it like the screen: gold in the middle, then red, then blue. Put a tape line on the floor. Pick your throwers. They throw soft balls at the paper target, one at a time. Tap the screen where each ball hit. Pick up the balls only when the teacher says, after everyone has thrown.
Follow the steps on the card. Then press Close.
Let's learn to throw like Bo. Press Show me, then try it with Bo.
Let's do a throwing test! Tap a question card.
Throw at the paper target! Then tap the screen where each ball hit.

Bring your arm way back, elbow up.

Follow through across your body, toward the target.
Step with your left foot, the opposite foot.
Step with your right foot, the opposite foot.
Throw with your right hand. Step with your left foot.
Throw with your left hand. Step with your right foot.
Now you try! Press Throw with Bo to throw together.
Ready, aim...
Great throwing! Press Throw with Bo to go again.
Make a guess! Hold up one finger for Way A, or two fingers for Way B.
Make two tape lines: three giant steps from the wall and six giant steps from the wall.
Pick your throwers. Each one throws once, one at a time. Tap where each ball hits.
Same throwers, same order, same line. Only the feet change. Tap where each ball hits.
Same throwers, same order, same line. Only the eyes change. Tap where each ball hits.
Same throwers, same order, same target. Only the line changes. Tap where each ball hits.
Same throwers, same order, same line. Only the target changes. Tap where each ball hits.
Way A is done! Press Start Way B.
Which way got more hits? Tell a friend. Then press Show the answer.
Press Test again to throw again, or New question for a new test.

Coaches teach the step because it helps your whole body push the ball and aim it.
Good throwers look at the target the whole time.
Closer is easier to hit. Step back to the far line when you are ready for a challenge.
